tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__get_issue
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about an issue by ID, including attachments, git branch name, and active Triage Intelligence suggestions when the issue is in triage. A nonempty fields selection overrides the include options; request optional fields directly in fields.

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

fields.description: Fields to include in each result. Explicitly requested fields with no value return null. `id` is always included. Omit or pass an empty array for the default response.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_comments
tools.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. `statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page

cursor.description: Omit for the first page. To continue, pass the previous response's cursor when hasNextPage is true

orderBy.description: Timestamp to sort results by: creation time or last update time

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Set only together with `statusUpdateId`; omit for issue, project, initiative, document, and milestone comments. Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__list_issue_statuses
tools.description: List available issue statuses in a Linear team

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue
tools.description: Create or update a Linear issue. If `id` is provided, updates the existing issue; otherwise creates a new one. When creating, `team` is required, and `title` is required unless `template` is set. Note: use `assignee` (not `assigneeId`) to set the assignee — it accepts a user ID, name, email, or "me".

id.description: Only for updating an existing issue. Pass the issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Do NOT pass this parameter when creating a new issue.

title.description: Issue title (required when creating, unless template is set)

description.description: Content as Markdown. Do not escape the string — use literal newlines and special characters, not escape sequences. To mention a user, use @displayName (e.g., @johndoe)

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__claude_ai_Notion__notion-fetch
tools.description:
Retrieves details about a Notion entity (page, database, data source, or saved database view) by URL or ID.

Provide a URL or ID in `id`. Make multiple calls for multiple entities.

For pages, use path, verification, edit time, and truncation metadata to assess the source. Treat recency as context, not proof. Report material uncertainty when sources conflict.

Pages use Notion-flavored Markdown. For the complete specification, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool.

Pass a `notion://docs/*` URI as `id` to read that MCP documentation resource.

Databases return data sources in `<data-source url="collection://...">` tags. Fetch the collection:// URL for its schema and use it with update_data_source or query_data_sources. Multi-source databases return more than one data source.

Saved views return filters, sorts, and display settings. To query their rows, use query_data_sources with `mode: "view"`.

A null cover or icon means none; an omitted one means unavailable, not absent. Keep a page's Markdown icon attribute for edit round trips. File URLs expire; re-fetch to refresh them. Uploaded media blocks use stable `notion-file-block://` sources; keep them when editing or copying Markdown. Get download URLs with get_file_download_urls, or set `include_file_urls` to true for a `references` map. Before relying on page content, check `truncated`, `unknown_block_count`, and `unknown_block_ids` for omitted subtrees.

Set `include_discussions` to true for discussion counts, markers, previews, and `discussion://` URLs that correlate with get_comments.

id.description: The ID or URL of the Notion page, database, or data source to fetch. Supports notion.so URLs, Notion Sites URLs (*.notion.site), raw UUIDs, and data source URLs (collection://...). Pass "memory" to fetch the connected user's About page and memory database in this workspace without creating them. Pass a notion://docs/* URI to read that documentation resource. Also accepts an explicit saved view URL (view://...) from a database response. If a database block ID returns a validation error, use the collection:// URL from that error. Example: <example>notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec</example>.

include_transcript.description: Whether to include meeting note transcripts. Defaults to false. When true, full transcripts are included; when false, a placeholder with the meeting note URL is shown instead.

include_discussions.description: Whether to include discussion/comment indicators in the page output. When true, adds a <page-discussions> summary with discussion count, preview snippets, and discussion:// URLs. Use with the get_comments tool to retrieve full discussion content. Defaults to false.

include_file_urls.description: Whether to return signed download URLs for uploaded files. Defaults to false. When false, page Markdown cites uploaded files by stable notion-file-block:// references and the response has no references map; call get_file_download_urls with the references when you need those files' contents. When true, the response's references map gives the signed URL for each reference.

instructions_version.description: Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.

skill.description: For tracking only: the name of the agent skill you are following for this task, such as notion-meeting-prep. Omit if you are not following a skill.

content.text: Tool loaded.

input.message:
SMA-803 owner here: the ToolDeferred variant is not final yet; my spec is at the draft stage.

1. I own SMA-803 (deferred tool calls). I am session for branch feature/sma-803-deferred-tool-calls-a-defer-decision-ends, worktree .claude/worktrees/sma-803-deferred-tool-calls. SMA-804 is not mine.

2. Planned shape, from ADR-15 and ADR-0028 (g): SessionEvent::ToolDeferred holds call_id, the tool name, the effective args (after PreToolUse and Replace), the active agent name, a prompt, and ts. The serde tag will follow the existing snake_case convention, so "tool_deferred". For project(): my current intent is that the ToolCalled stays in the projected history and ToolDeferred adds no Item, so a resume can append the resolved ToolResult after it. This is NOT final. The field names and the project() rule can change at the spec gate (Sven approves). I will send you a second message when Sven approves the spec, with the exact definition.

3. I do not plan to edit crates/paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit, release-plz.toml, or any session backend Cargo.toml. I edit core (session event, permissions, loop, run result) and probably runtime-temporal (Defer → Deny). If a backend needs a code change for the new variant (for example an exhaustive match), I will tell you first. Please add the ToolDeferred conformance test on your side, after my variant lands.

4. Not decided yet. The default is to leave the bump to release-plz. A hand bump is only necessary if another crate in my PR uses new core API and must publish in the same release (CLAUDE.md rule). If runtime-temporal uses a new core variant, that rule applies, and I will tell you before I push.

  **Authorization pipeline for one tool call.** The per-call future is in `run_tools_concurrent`, `core/src/agent.rs:521-665`. It calls `Interceptors::authorize` (control.rs:116), which delegates to `RunContext::authorize_tool` (context.rs:469). Condensed:
  ```
  1. interceptors.fire(HookEvent::PreToolUse{tool,args})          // agent_hooks first, then ctx.hooks() registry; first Deny short-circuits
     Deny -> ToolCallOutcome{ Err("blocked by PreToolUse hook: ..") } ; ReplaceInput -> args replaced
  2. authorize_tool(name, effect, &args):
     a. deny_rules any match               -> Deny{"denied by deny rule: {tool}"}
     b. guard rules (built-in destructive_defaults() if default_guards, then user guard_rules), in order:
          Deny -> Deny
          Ask  -> no handler => Deny{"destructive command requires approval: .."}
                  handler.decide(): Allow => `continue` (clears THIS guard only), Deny => Deny
     c. allow_rules any match              -> Allow          // short-circuits mode AND policy, in every mode
     d. mode: Bypass->Allow; Plan && effect!=ReadOnly->Deny; AcceptEdits && effect==Write->Allow; DontAsk->Deny; else fall through
     e. policy: None -> Allow; Some(p) -> p.check(ctx,tool,args)
     f. AskUser{prompt}: no handler -> Deny{"no approval handler installed"}; else handler.decide(tool,&prompt,args) -> Allow|Deny
          other (Allow/Deny/Replace) passed through
  3. match decision: Allow {} | Replace{args}=>args=sanitized | Deny/AskUser => push AgentEvent::PermissionDenied{tool,reason} into a Mutex<Vec>, outcome Err("permission denied: {reason}")
  4. invoke tool (None -> Err("unknown tool: {name}"))
  5. PostToolUse hook (Deny -> Err("blocked by PostToolUse hook: ..."), ReplaceOutput replaces JSON)
  6. finalize_tool_output(json, redact_output, secrets)           // redaction is the last transform
  ```
  - The durable/hook-free version is `execute_tool_call` (`core/src/tool_exec.rs:50-116`): resolve, `authorize_tool`, invoke, `finalize_tool_output`. It returns `(ToolCallOutcome, Option<AgentEvent::PermissionDenied>)`.
  - The Temporal `invoke_tool_inner` (`runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs:~125`) drops that event.
  - The loop gathers `denied` events from `run_tools_concurrent` and yields them after all tools finish (agent.rs:1022-1024), not at the moment of denial.

    - `TransitionOutcome{next_state,events,next_action,conversation_appends}`.
    - `pub fn transition(&LoopState, TransitionInput, &TransitionCtx) -> TransitionOutcome` is a pure function, a single `match (state, input)`. It ends in a catch-all `(s,i)` arm that yields `Failed(Other("invalid transition"))`.
  
  **Main loop** — `impl Agent for LlmAgent`, `core/src/agent.rs:681-1149`. Inside `async_stream::stream!`:
  - Seed `conversation = [Item::System(instructions)] ++ input.messages` (:724-730).
  - `loop_state = CallingModel{turn:0}`, `tx_input = Start` (:732-733).
  - Yields `RunStarted`, then does the handoff-name collision check.
  - Fires `OnRunStart` (`HookDenied` fails the run) and runs input guardrails (tripwire gives `GuardrailTriggered` + `RunFailed`).
  - Then `loop {}` (:822):
    1. `transition(...)`.
    2. Output guardrail gate if the next state is `Done` (:836-856).
    3. Yield the events (`TurnStarted` fires `OnTurnStart` hook and starts a turn span).
    4. `loop_state = next_state`, then extend `conversation` with `conversation_appends`.
    5. `match next_action`:
       - **CallModel** (:913): apply `pending_injections` as `Item::System`, `model.invoke`, stream deltas as `AgentEvent`s, `ModelTurnAccumulator.finish()`, `conversation.extend(items)`, `tx_input = ModelResponse`.
       - **ExecuteTools** (:1010): `ctx.to_tool_context()`, then `run_tools_concurrent`. That is **concurrent**: `join_all`, or `.buffered(n)` if `parallel_tool_call_limit` is set. It then yields the `denied` events, and for each outcome (in call order) pushes `Item::ToolResult{call_id, content: Ok|Err-as-Text}` onto `conversation`. Finally `tx_input = ToolResults{outcomes}`. The next `transition` emits `ToolOutputItem` events, bumps turn to `turn+1`, and emits `TurnStarted`.
       - **Terminate** (:1035): fires `OnRunComplete`; if `loop_state` is `Failed(err)` it does `failure.set(err)`; then `return`.
       - **Handoff** (:1048): see below.
  - **Turn boundaries:** `TurnStarted{turn}` is emitted by `transition`. After `ToolResults`, `next_turn = turn+1`.
  - **Max turns:** `RunConfig.max_turns`, default 16.
    - `transition` fails with `MaxTurnsExceeded` if `turn >= max_turns` at `CallingModel` (loop_state.rs:~170), or `next_turn >= max_turns` after tool results (:~425).
    - The effective config is `ctx.run_config().cloned().unwrap_or(self.config)` (agent.rs:691).
    - A structured-output `Finalizing` turn uses `turn+1`.
  - **Handoff:** the model's tool call matching a `HandoffDef.tool_name` takes precedence over regular calls (loop_state.rs ~215-248) and gives `ApplyingHandoff`.
    - The driver does `child = ctx.handoff_child()` and fails if `child.agent_depth() > max_agent_depth` (`MaxAgentDepthExceeded`).
    - It fires the `OnHandoff` hook (a Deny gives `HookDenied`).
    - It yields `HandoffItem{from,to}` then `AgentUpdated{agent}`.
    - It runs `target_agent.run(child, AgentInput{messages: transcript})` and forwards the sub-stream. `RunStarted` is dropped, `RunCompleted` usage is summed with `parent_usage`, and everything else is passed through.
    - It fires `OnSubagentStop` and then **returns**.
    - The active agent is not swapped inside a loop. It is a nested run whose events are forwarded.
    - The handoff transcript is built by `thread_handoff_transcript(conversation)`.
  - **Workflow agents** (`workflow.rs:163,333,523`, `graph.rs:242`, `swarm.rs:288`) use `subagent_child()` and forward events with `other => yield other`. They intercept only `RunStarted`/`RunCompleted`/`RunFailed`/`MessageOutput` (and `HandoffItem` in swarm) and pass everything else through. Any new terminal-like event would therefore be forwarded unmodified, but none of these combinators would stop on it.
  - **`AgentAsTool`** (`core/src/agent_as_tool.rs:94-196`):
    - Depth check is `ctx.agent_depth()+1 > ctx.max_agent_depth()` (`ToolContext` carries both), else `MaxAgentDepthExceeded` wrapped in `ToolError::Other`.
    - It builds an isolated `RunContext` (fresh `MemorySession`, empty hooks) with `.with_agent_depth(depth+1)` and the parent permission config copied.
    - It runs `agent.run(sub_ctx, AgentInput::from_user_text(input))`, then `RunResultStreaming::with_failure(..).collect()`, fires the parent's `OnSubagentStop` hooks via a `fire_ctx`, and returns `ToolOutput(Value::String(final_output))`.
    - The sub-run's own `RunConfig` does not inherit the parent's.
  - **Depth field:** `RunContext.agent_depth: u32` (context.rs:~66), accessor `agent_depth()`. `max_agent_depth` lives in `RunConfig` (default 8).

  **Authorization pipeline for one tool call.** The per-call future is in `run_tools_concurrent`, `core/src/agent.rs:521-665`. It calls `Interceptors::authorize` (control.rs:116), which delegates to `RunContext::authorize_tool` (context.rs:469). Condensed:
  ```
  1. interceptors.fire(HookEvent::PreToolUse{tool,args})          // agent_hooks first, then ctx.hooks() registry; first Deny short-circuits
     Deny -> ToolCallOutcome{ Err("blocked by PreToolUse hook: ..") } ; ReplaceInput -> args replaced
  2. authorize_tool(name, effect, &args):
     a. deny_rules any match               -> Deny{"denied by deny rule: {tool}"}
     b. guard rules (built-in destructive_defaults() if default_guards, then user guard_rules), in order:
          Deny -> Deny
          Ask  -> no handler => Deny{"destructive command requires approval: .."}
                  handler.decide(): Allow => `continue` (clears THIS guard only), Deny => Deny
     c. allow_rules any match              -> Allow          // short-circuits mode AND policy, in every mode
     d. mode: Bypass->Allow; Plan && effect!=ReadOnly->Deny; AcceptEdits && effect==Write->Allow; DontAsk->Deny; else fall through
     e. policy: None -> Allow; Some(p) -> p.check(ctx,tool,args)
     f. AskUser{prompt}: no handler -> Deny{"no approval handler installed"}; else handler.decide(tool,&prompt,args) -> Allow|Deny
          other (Allow/Deny/Replace) passed through
  3. match decision: Allow {} | Replace{args}=>args=sanitized | Deny/AskUser => push AgentEvent::PermissionDenied{tool,reason} into a Mutex<Vec>, outcome Err("permission denied: {reason}")
  4. invoke tool (None -> Err("unknown tool: {name}"))
  5. PostToolUse hook (Deny -> Err("blocked by PostToolUse hook: ..."), ReplaceOutput replaces JSON)
  6. finalize_tool_output(json, redact_output, secrets)           // redaction is the last transform
  ```
  - The durable/hook-free version is `execute_tool_call` (`core/src/tool_exec.rs:50-116`): resolve, `authorize_tool`, invoke, `finalize_tool_output`. It returns `(ToolCallOutcome, Option<AgentEvent::PermissionDenied>)`.
  - The Temporal `invoke_tool_inner` (`runtime-temporal/src/activities.rs:~125`) drops that event.
  - The loop gathers `denied` events from `run_tools_concurrent` and yields them after all tools finish (agent.rs:1022-1024), not at the moment of denial.

    - `NextAction` is `CallModel{request} | ExecuteTools{calls} | Terminate | Handoff`, non_exhaustive.

    - `TransitionOutcome{next_state,events,next_action,conversation_appends}`.
    - `pub fn transition(&LoopState, TransitionInput, &TransitionCtx) -> TransitionOutcome` is a pure function, a single `match (state, input)`. It ends in a catch-all `(s,i)` arm that yields `Failed(Other("invalid transition"))`.
  
  **Main loop** — `impl Agent for LlmAgent`, `core/src/agent.rs:681-1149`. Inside `async_stream::stream!`:
  - Seed `conversation = [Item::System(instructions)] ++ input.messages` (:724-730).
  - `loop_state = CallingModel{turn:0}`, `tx_input = Start` (:732-733).
  - Yields `RunStarted`, then does the handoff-name collision check.
  - Fires `OnRunStart` (`HookDenied` fails the run) and runs input guardrails (tripwire gives `GuardrailTriggered` + `RunFailed`).
  - Then `loop {}` (:822):
    1. `transition(...)`.
    2. Output guardrail gate if the next state is `Done` (:836-856).
    3. Yield the events (`TurnStarted` fires `OnTurnStart` hook and starts a turn span).
    4. `loop_state = next_state`, then extend `conversation` with `conversation_appends`.
    5. `match next_action`:
       - **CallModel** (:913): apply `pending_injections` as `Item::System`, `model.invoke`, stream deltas as `AgentEvent`s, `ModelTurnAccumulator.finish()`, `conversation.extend(items)`, `tx_input = ModelResponse`.
       - **ExecuteTools** (:1010): `ctx.to_tool_context()`, then `run_tools_concurrent`. That is **concurrent**: `join_all`, or `.buffered(n)` if `parallel_tool_call_limit` is set. It then yields the `denied` events, and for each outcome (in call order) pushes `Item::ToolResult{call_id, content: Ok|Err-as-Text}` onto `conversation`. Finally `tx_input = ToolResults{outcomes}`. The next `transition` emits `ToolOutputItem` events, bumps turn to `turn+1`, and emits `TurnStarted`.
       - **Terminate** (:1035): fires `OnRunComplete`; if `loop_state` is `Failed(err)` it does `failure.set(err)`; then `return`.
       - **Handoff** (:1048): see below.
  - **Turn boundaries:** `TurnStarted{turn}` is emitted by `transition`. After `ToolResults`, `next_turn = turn+1`.
  - **Max turns:** `RunConfig.max_turns`, default 16.
    - `transition` fails with `MaxTurnsExceeded` if `turn >= max_turns` at `CallingModel` (loop_state.rs:~170), or `next_turn >= max_turns` after tool results (:~425).
    - The effective config is `ctx.run_config().cloned().unwrap_or(self.config)` (agent.rs:691).
    - A structured-output `Finalizing` turn uses `turn+1`.
  - **Handoff:** the model's tool call matching a `HandoffDef.tool_name` takes precedence over regular calls (loop_state.rs ~215-248) and gives `ApplyingHandoff`.
    - The driver does `child = ctx.handoff_child()` and fails if `child.agent_depth() > max_agent_depth` (`MaxAgentDepthExceeded`).
    - It fires the `OnHandoff` hook (a Deny gives `HookDenied`).
    - It yields `HandoffItem{from,to}` then `AgentUpdated{agent}`.
    - It runs `target_agent.run(child, AgentInput{messages: transcript})` and forwards the sub-stream. `RunStarted` is dropped, `RunCompleted` usage is summed with `parent_usage`, and everything else is passed through.
    - It fires `OnSubagentStop` and then **returns**.
    - The active agent is not swapped inside a loop. It is a nested run whose events are forwarded.
    - The handoff transcript is built by `thread_handoff_transcript(conversation)`.
  - **Workflow agents** (`workflow.rs:163,333,523`, `graph.rs:242`, `swarm.rs:288`) use `subagent_child()` and forward events with `other => yield other`. They intercept only `RunStarted`/`RunCompleted`/`RunFailed`/`MessageOutput` (and `HandoffItem` in swarm) and pass everything else through. Any new terminal-like event would therefore be forwarded unmodified, but none of these combinators would stop on it.
  - **`AgentAsTool`** (`core/src/agent_as_tool.rs:94-196`):
    - Depth check is `ctx.agent_depth()+1 > ctx.max_agent_depth()` (`ToolContext` carries both), else `MaxAgentDepthExceeded` wrapped in `ToolError::Other`.
    - It builds an isolated `RunContext` (fresh `MemorySession`, empty hooks) with `.with_agent_depth(depth+1)` and the parent permission config copied.
    - It runs `agent.run(sub_ctx, AgentInput::from_user_text(input))`, then `RunResultStreaming::with_failure(..).collect()`, fires the parent's `OnSubagentStop` hooks via a `fire_ctx`, and returns `ToolOutput(Value::String(final_output))`.
    - The sub-run's own `RunConfig` does not inherit the parent's.
  - **Depth field:** `RunContext.agent_depth: u32` (context.rs:~66), accessor `agent_depth()`. `max_agent_depth` lives in `RunConfig` (default 8).

I now have a map of the current code. Here is what I understand, and what I found.

**Your request, in my words.** A permission check can return `Defer` instead of blocking on the `ApprovalHandler` future. The loop runs the other allowed calls of that turn, then ends the run with `StopReason::Deferred { calls }`. The session records a `ToolDeferred` event with the effective args. A later run takes `Approved` or `Denied` per `call_id`, checks the call again, and writes all results before any new input. The always-on host (SMA-795) needs this, so that an approval that takes hours does not hold a lease.

**What I found that changes the design:**

1. **"Depth > 0 is Deny" conflicts with handoffs.** `handoff_child()` also adds 1 to `agent_depth`. A literal depth rule would deny every deferral after a handoff, but the ADR wants handoffs to defer. My proposal: a `RunContext` flag that says whether deferral is allowed. The runner sets it (`TokioRunner` sets it on, `TemporalRunner` leaves it off). A handoff child keeps it. `subagent_child()` (workflow agents) and the `AgentAsTool` sub-context turn it off. A run with the flag off treats `Defer` as `Deny`.
2. **The stop reason needs a new terminal event.** If I add a field to `RunCompleted`, callers break. My proposal: a new terminal variant `AgentEvent::RunDeferred { calls, usage }`. `is_terminal` includes it, and `collect()` maps it to `StopReason::Deferred`.
3. **Session order is a trap.** Today the runner records the new input *before* the loop starts. In that case the resolved results land after the new user message, and providers reject that order. The recorder must put the resolution results first.
4. **The handoff case needs the agent path.** The root agent can only see its direct handoff targets, so a resume for agent C behind A→B→C needs the chain. My proposal: `PendingToolCall` records the handoff path, not only the active agent.

**The open question that changes the build most: how a caller resumes.**

- **A. Resolutions on `AgentInput` (my pick).** The caller does `runner.run(agent, ctx, AgentInput::new().with_resolutions(r), cfg)`. `run` and `run_streamed` both work, and the `Runner` trait gets no new method. The risk: a runner that does not know about resolutions ignores them. I make `TemporalRunner` reject them explicitly.
- **B. New `Runner::resume_deferred` and `resume_deferred_streamed` methods**, with default implementations that return an "unsupported" error. This API is more explicit, but it adds two trait methods and a second path that the code must keep in line with `run`.

Which way do you want to go? Also tell me if any of points 1–4 is wrong.

input.message:
SMA-803 proposal for the terminal event: one new terminal variant per stop reason, no new field on RunCompleted. This is pending Sven's approval at my spec gate.

1. A new variant. Variant-level fields on AgentEvent are not non_exhaustive (only the enum is), so a new field on RunCompleted breaks callers that build or destructure it. Plan: AgentEvent::RunDeferred { calls: Vec<PendingToolCall>, usage: TokenUsage } for SMA-803. For SMA-804 I suggest the same pattern: AgentEvent::RunStopped { reason: String, usage: TokenUsage }. is_terminal() = RunCompleted | RunFailed | RunDeferred | RunStopped. I add RunDeferred; you add RunStopped and its is_terminal arm after the rebase. The every_variant test with the hardcoded count (agent.rs ~1566) changes in both PRs.

2. final_output for a non-completed run: collect() returns Ok, with final_output = the text of the last MessageOutput (as today, empty if none), and stop_reason = Deferred/Stopped from the terminal event. collect() sets stop_reason Completed only on RunCompleted. collect_typed / parse_final: my proposal is that collect_typed returns Err for a non-completed stop reason, with a new RunError variant (RunError::Incomplete { stop_reason }, RunError is non_exhaustive), because there is no structured output to parse. parse_final on a RunResult with a non-Completed stop reason returns the same error. Not final; I tell you if Sven changes it.

3. Yes. The handoff re-yield forwards the child's RunDeferred with the child's usage plus parent_usage, like RunCompleted today. Please do the same for RunStopped. So a Stop in a handoff child ends the whole run with Stopped.

Your assumptions match mine for Deferred too: no output guardrails, no LoopState::Done, OnRunComplete fires once as today. For Deferred I plan a new LoopState path: ExecutingTools → NeedsApproval { pending } → Terminate, with the RunDeferred event.

---
name: project_release_ascend_needs_core_bump
description: "When a 0.0.0 stub crate ascends and uses paigasus-helikon-core API added in the same PR, you must also bump core's version or release-plz's publish fails."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6a9723cd-b6b1-44aa-a8bf-8c53c21a6501
---

The CLAUDE.md "4-step ascend recipe" (bump stub `0.0.0`→`0.1.0`, drop `publish = false`, remove the `release = false` block in `release-plz.toml`, bump the `[workspace.dependencies]` pin) is INSUFFICIENT when the ascending crate depends on `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR. `cargo publish --verify` builds the ascending crate's tarball against the **registry** core (the `path` is stripped at publish), so if the published core version lacks the new API the publish fails with compile errors (E0599/E0609 "no field/method/variant") → "failed to verify package tarball", and release-plz's combined job (SMA-351) aborts before its release-PR step → deadlock (core never gets an auto bump).

**Why:** release-plz publishes per Cargo.toml-version-vs-crates.io diff and ignores source changes that don't bump the version; a squashed PR commit scoped `feat(<ascending-crate>)` attributes nothing to core, so crates.io core stays at its old version without the new API.

**How to apply:** In the ascend PR, ALSO bump `paigasus-helikon-core` (patch for additive/non-breaking-behind-`#[non_exhaustive]`, e.g. `0.2.0`→`0.2.1`, matching release-plz's 0.x convention) plus its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin + CHANGELOG. release-plz then publishes core first, then the ascending crate (dependency-ordered) verifies against the fresh core. Diagnosed in SMA-321: PR #45 failed the release; PR #46 (`chore(release)` bumping core to 0.2.1) fixed it. Related: [[reference_crates_io_api_user_agent]] (preflight version checks need a custom UA).

**Complement — the manual bump is ONLY for the deadlock above; do NOT over-apply it to an already-released consumer.** The deadlock requires a crate whose Cargo.toml version is bumped *by hand* in the PR (the ascend `0.0.0`→`0.1.0`, or any manual bump), forcing release-plz's `release` step to publish it immediately — before release-plz has bumped core. If the consuming crate is **already released** (a real version, not a stub) and you do NOT hand-bump it, NOTHING publishes prematurely: release-plz bundles core + consumer + facade into one release PR and publishes them in dependency order (core lands on the registry before the consumer's `cargo publish --verify`), with the `dependencies_update` cascade to the facade intact. So for an already-released consumer adding+using same-PR core API, the correct play is **pure-auto** (no manual version/CHANGELOG edits at all) — and a manual same-PR core bump would actually *defeat* the cascade (the documented facade-drift second-order caveat). Reactive fallback if a publish ever deadlocks: a follow-up `chore(release):` PR (the SMA-321/SMA-346 pattern). Decided AND confirmed in SMA-418 (PR #80, `paigasus-helikon-tools` already at `0.1.2`): the ticket initially pattern-matched the ascend ritual; we shipped pure-auto instead. On merge, release-plz opened one `chore: release` PR (#81) bumping core `0.5.1→0.5.2`, tools `0.1.2→0.1.3`, AND every other core-dependent via the cascade (facade `0.3.8→0.3.9`, providers-openai/anthropic, sessions-sqlite, runtime-tokio, mcp — each a patch bump to refresh its core req); merging #81 published all of them to crates.io cleanly in dependency order (core first), no deadlock, no manual bump. So for an already-released consumer, pure-auto is the proven path — and note the cascade touches the WHOLE workspace (everything depends on core), which a by-hand bump can't replicate consistently.

# SMA-803: Deferred tool calls — design

- **Issue:** [SMA-803](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-803)
- **Design sources:** Helikon ADR-15 ("Deferred tool calls and a turn-boundary
  checkpoint") and paigasus-core ADR-0028, decision (g).
- **Related work:** SMA-804 (turn-boundary checkpoint, shares `StopReason`),
  SMA-805 (publishes `sessions-testkit`, adds a `ToolDeferred` conformance test),
  SMA-795 and SMA-793 (consumers in paigasus-core).

## 1. Intent

A permission check can defer a tool call. The run then ends cleanly at the turn
boundary. A later run resumes the call with the approver's answer.

Today an ask blocks the loop on an `ApprovalHandler` future, and
`LoopState::NeedsApproval` returns `NotImplemented`. The always-on agent host in
paigasus-core needs deferral. An approval can take hours. The host must not hold
a lease and a worker slot for that time.

## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals

**Goals**

- A policy, a guard `Ask` and an `AskUser` can all defer one call.
- A run with a deferred call ends with `StopReason::Deferred { calls }`. Its
  session holds one `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred` per deferred call, with the
  effective args.
- A resume with `Approved` runs the call once, with the recorded args, after a
  re-check. A resume with `Denied` records the denial result.
- The session log stays valid for every provider after a deferral and after a
  resume. Each `ToolCall` gets exactly one `ToolResult`, and the results come
  before any new user input.
- Every change is compile-compatible for callers (new variants and fields go
  only on `#[non_exhaustive]` types).

**Non-goals**

- Host-side storage, approval tokens, expiry and "superseded" rules. These are
  SMA-795.
- Deferral inside `AgentAsTool` sub-runs and inside workflow-agent children. In
  v1 a `Defer` there is a `Deny`.
- Deferral in `TemporalRunner`. In v1 a `Defer` there is a `Deny`.
- Support for `RunDeferred` in the HTTP runtimes (axum, actix, agentcore). They
  never opt in, so a `Defer` there is a `Deny` (see §4.2).
- The turn-boundary checkpoint and `StopReason::Stopped`. These are SMA-804.

**Anti-goals** (the design fails if one of these occurs, even when it works)

- An approved call runs with args that are different from the args that the
  approver saw.
- A `Deny` from any stage is overridden by an approval.
- A session log has a `ToolCall` without a `ToolResult`, or a `ToolResult` after
  a later user message. Providers reject such a log.
- A run that did not opt in to deferral ends with `Deferred`.

## 3. Approaches

The open choice was how a caller resumes a deferred run.

- **A. Resolutions on `AgentInput` (chosen by Sven).** The caller calls the
  usual `Runner::run` or `run_streamed` with
  `AgentInput::new().with_resolution(call_id, ToolResolution::Approved)`. The
  `Runner` trait gets no new method, and streaming works without extra code.
  Risk: a runner that does not know about resolutions ignores them.
  Mitigation: `TemporalRunner` rejects them explicitly, and `TokioRunner`
  rejects a run on a session with open deferrals that has no resolutions.
- **B. New `Runner::resume_deferred` and `resume_deferred_streamed` methods**,
  with defaults that return "unsupported". The API is more explicit. But it adds
  two trait methods and a second path that must stay in line with `run`.

## 4. Design

### 4.1 Public types (all in `paigasus-helikon-core`)

The exact names are the builder's call (ADR-0028 §8). The names below are the
working names that SMA-804 and SMA-805 already use, so change them only for a
strong reason, and tell those sessions.

- `PermissionDecision::Defer { prompt: String }`.
- `ApprovalOutcome::Defer`. An `ApprovalHandler` returns it to defer a guard
  `Ask` or an `AskUser`. The prompt is the prompt of that ask point.
- `PendingToolCall` (`#[non_exhaustive]` struct, `Clone`, `Debug`, `PartialEq`,
  serde): `call_id`, `tool`, `args` (effective args), `prompt`, `agent` (the
  agent that made the call), and `handoff_path: Vec<String>` (the agent names
  from the root agent to `agent`, both included). Give it a constructor and
  accessors, because callers outside core cannot use a struct literal.
- `ToolResolution` (`#[non_exhaustive]` enum): `Approved` and
  `Denied { reason: String }`.
- `StopReason` (`#[non_exhaustive]` enum, `Clone`, `Debug`, `PartialEq`,
  `Default = Completed`): `Completed` and `Deferred { calls: Vec<PendingToolCall> }`.
  SMA-804 adds `Stopped { reason: String }`.
- `RunResult` gets `pub stop_reason: StopReason`. `RunResult` is
  `#[non_exhaustive]` and derives `Default`, so this is compatible.
- `AgentEvent::RunDeferred { calls: Vec<PendingToolCall>, usage: TokenUsage }`.
  It is a terminal event: `is_terminal()` returns `true` for it. Do not add a
  field to `RunCompleted`, because variant fields are not `#[non_exhaustive]`.
  SMA-804 adds `RunStopped { reason, usage }` with the same pattern.
- `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred { call_id, name, args, prompt, agent,
  handoff_path, ts }`, serde tag `"tool_deferred"`. `kind()`, `ts()` and
  `project()` get the new arm. `project()` adds no `Item` for it
  (contribution 0, as for `HandoffOccurred`).
- `RunError::Incomplete { stop_reason: StopReason }` and
  `RunError::InvalidResume { reason: String }`. `RunError` is
  `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- `RunContext::with_deferred_tool_calls(bool)` and
  `deferred_tool_calls_enabled() -> bool` (see §4.2).
- `AgentInput` gets the resolutions that the caller sets
  (`with_resolution(call_id, ToolResolution)`), and a runner-only part that
  carries the matched pending calls and the new input (§4.6). `AgentInput` is
  `#[non_exhaustive]`.

### 4.2 Who may defer

A `RunContext` has a flag "deferred tool calls enabled". The default is `false`.

- The caller turns it on with `with_deferred_tool_calls(true)`. The host does
  this. Nobody else needs it.
- `handoff_child()` keeps the flag. A handoff child is part of the top-level
  loop, so it can defer.
- `subagent_child()` (workflow agents) and the `AgentAsTool` sub-context set the
  flag to `false`. This replaces the ADR's "depth > 0" rule. Reason:
  `handoff_child()` also adds 1 to `agent_depth`, so a depth rule would deny
  every deferral after a handoff.
- `TemporalRunner` sets the flag to `false` on the context that it receives. Its
  worker builds its own context, which has the default `false`.
- `to_tool_context()` and the `AgentAsTool` copy site must not copy the flag
  as `true`. Write a regression test in `core/tests/subagent_propagation.rs`.
  This is one of the four `RunContext` copy sites that every new field must
  pass through.

When the flag is `false`, every point that would produce `Defer` produces
`Deny { reason: "approval deferred, but this run cannot defer: {prompt}" }`
instead. The exact text is the builder's call.

Reason for opt-in (my call): six runtimes use `TokioRunner` (axum, actix,
agentcore, evals, cli, mcp). Their run status knows only `RunCompleted` and
`RunFailed`. An opt-in keeps them correct with no change.

### 4.3 Authorization with `Defer`

`RunContext::authorize_tool` keeps its stage order: deny rules › guard rules ›
allow rules › mode › policy › approval handler. "One deferral answers every ask
point of one call" means:

1. A guard `Ask` calls the handler. `Allow` clears this guard (as today).
   `Deny` returns `Deny`. `Defer` sets a "deferred" mark with the guard's
   prompt, and the pipeline continues.
2. After a guard sets the mark, later guard `Ask` points do not call the handler
   again. They count as deferred too.
3. A later `Deny` from any stage returns `Deny` (a guard `Deny`, mode `Plan` or
   `DontAsk`, a policy `Deny`).
4. A policy `AskUser` with the mark set does not call the handler. A policy
   `AskUser` without the mark calls the handler, and `Defer` sets the mark. A
   policy `Defer` sets the mark.
5. A policy `Replace { args }` with the mark set: the result is `Defer`, and the
   pending call records the replaced args as its effective args. The approver
   sees the replaced args.
6. At the end: with the mark set, and no `Deny`, the result is
   `Defer { prompt }`. The prompt is the first deferred ask point's prompt.
   Otherwise the result is as today.
7. An allow rule short-circuits mode and policy, as today. With the mark set,
   the result is `Defer`, not `Allow`.

`AskUser` without a handler is still `Deny` ("no approval handler installed").
A policy `Defer` needs no handler.

`authorize_tool` itself returns `Defer` only when the flag (§4.2) is on.
Otherwise it maps the deferral to `Deny`, as §4.2 says. `execute_tool_call`
(`tool_exec.rs`, the durable path) always maps `Defer` to `Deny`.

The matches without a wildcard in core (`agent.rs` `run_tools_concurrent`,
`tool_exec.rs`, both `ApprovalOutcome` matches in `context.rs`) change with the
new variants.

### 4.4 The loop: a turn with deferred calls

In `run_tools_concurrent`, a call whose decision is `Defer` is not invoked. It
returns a "deferred" outcome that holds a `PendingToolCall`: the `call_id`, the
tool name, the effective args (after `PreToolUse` and any `Replace`), the
prompt, the current agent name, and the handoff path (§4.7). The other calls of
the turn run as today. Their results go into the conversation as today.

When a turn has one or more deferred calls:

- The loop does not call the model again.
- The transition moves to `LoopState::NeedsApproval { pending }` and then to
  `NextAction::Terminate`. `pending` keeps its current type
  (`Vec<ToolCallRequest>`); the full data travels in the events.
- The events, in order: the `ToolOutputItem` of each call that ran, the
  `PermissionDenied` events as today, one `ApprovalRequested { call_id, tool,
  args }` per deferred call (this variant exists and is never emitted today),
  then `RunDeferred { calls, usage }`.
- The output guardrails do not run. `OnRunComplete` fires once, as on every
  `Terminate`.
- A handoff in the same model response takes precedence over regular calls, as
  today. So a turn never has both a handoff and a deferral.

`TransitionInput::ToolResults { outcomes }` must stay compile-compatible, because
`runtime-temporal`'s driver constructs it. Add a new `TransitionInput` variant
for "results plus deferred calls", or an equivalent. This is the builder's call.
`transition()`'s existing arm `(NeedsApproval, _) => not_implemented("approval")`
goes away. `NeedsApproval` is now a terminal state.

### 4.5 Recording a deferral

- `SessionRecorder::observe` maps `RunDeferred` to one
  `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred` per call. It does not record `ApprovalRequested`.
- `SessionRecorder::drain` does not write a synthetic result for a call that has
  a `ToolDeferred` in this run.
- `TokioRunner::run_streamed` finalizes before it yields `RunDeferred`, because
  `is_terminal()` includes it.
- `RunResultStreaming::collect()` returns `Ok`. `final_output` is the text of
  the last `MessageOutput` (as today, empty if there is none).
  `stop_reason` is `Deferred { calls }` from the event. `stop_reason` is
  `Completed` only after a `RunCompleted`.
- `collect_typed()` returns `Err(RunError::Incomplete { stop_reason })` when the
  stop reason is not `Completed`, because there is no structured output to
  parse. `parse_final()` returns the same error.
- `CompactingSession` does not compact while its log has an open deferral (a
  `ToolDeferred` without a later `ToolReturned` for the same `call_id`).
  Otherwise the summary can remove the deferred `ToolCall` item, and a resume
  cannot pair the result. My call.

The session log after a deferred turn with calls `a` (ran), `b` (deferred) and
`c` (ran):

```text
assistant_message?  tool_called a  tool_called b  tool_called c
tool_returned a  tool_returned c  tool_deferred b
```

### 4.6 Resume

The caller sends the resolutions with the normal run call:

```rust
let input = AgentInput::new()
    .with_resolution("call_b", ToolResolution::Approved);
let result = TokioRunner.run(&agent, ctx, input, config).await?;
```

New user messages in the same input are allowed. They go after the results.

**Runner steps (`TokioRunner`):**

1. Read `session.events(None)`. Find the open deferrals: `ToolDeferred` events
   that have no later `ToolReturned` for the same `call_id`.
2. Validate, before the agent starts. A failure returns
   `Err(RunError::InvalidResume { reason })`, and nothing is recorded:
   - There are open deferrals, but the input has no resolutions.
   - The input has resolutions, but there are no open deferrals.
   - A resolution names a `call_id` that is not open.
   - An open deferral has no resolution. All open calls of the deferred turn
     must be resolved together, else the log stays invalid.
   - The projected snapshot has no `ToolCall` item for an open call.
   - The first name of the handoff path is not `agent.name()`.
3. Give the agent the snapshot as history, the matched pairs
   (`PendingToolCall`, `ToolResolution`), and the new input messages as a
   separate part. The runner records the new input as it does today.
4. Run the agent. Finalize as today.

**Agent steps (`LlmAgent`), before the first model call:**

1. Route to the recorded agent (§4.7). The rest runs on that agent.
2. For each pair, in the order of the original calls:
   - `Denied { reason }`: the result is `Err("permission denied: {reason}")`.
     Emit `PermissionDenied`.
   - `Approved`: run the re-check (§4.8). If it passes, invoke the tool with the
     recorded args. Then fire `PostToolUse` and apply redaction, as for a normal
     call. If the re-check fails, the result is the denial, and the loop emits
     `PermissionDenied`.
3. Emit one `ToolOutputItem` per result. Push each result into the
   conversation.
4. Then append the new input messages to the conversation, and continue the loop
   with `CallingModel`. The turn count starts at 0, as for every run.

**Session order.** The runner records the new input before the stream starts.
So `SessionRecorder::drain` must put the `ToolReturned` events of the resolved
calls before the recorded input events. The recorder knows the resolved
`call_id`s from the runner. If a resolved call has no result when the run ends
(the run was cancelled or timed out), `drain` writes the existing synthetic
result ("tool call did not complete (run cancelled/timed out)") for it, in the
same place before the input. This closes the deferral, so the log stays valid.

**Other runners.** `TemporalRunner` returns `RunError::InvalidResume` when the
input has resolutions. A third-party runner that ignores resolutions gives the
model a `ToolCall` without a result, and the provider returns an error. Document
this in the `Runner` trait docs.

**Agents other than `LlmAgent`.** A workflow agent that receives resolutions
returns `RunFailed` with "this agent cannot resume deferred calls". Its children
cannot defer (§4.2), so a valid session never needs this path.

### 4.7 Handoffs

- `RunContext` gets a handoff path (the agent names from the root to the
  current agent). `LlmAgent::run` adds its own name. The handoff child gets the
  path. The path goes into each `PendingToolCall`.
- On resume, the root agent compares the recorded path with its own name. If
  the path continues, it sends the run to the handoff target with the next name.
  It does not fire `OnHandoff` and does not emit `HandoffItem`, because the
  session already holds that handoff. It emits `AgentUpdated` so that the
  recorder knows the current agent.
- The child gets the **full** projected history, not
  `thread_handoff_transcript(...)`. That function removes every `ToolCall` and
  `ToolResult` item, so the deferred call would have no pair. Later normal runs
  also send the full history, so this is consistent.
- If an agent in the path is not a handoff target any more, the deepest agent
  that the path reaches resolves every pending call as
  `Denied { reason: "agent no longer available: {name}" }` and continues its own
  loop. The handoff re-yield adds the child usage to `parent_usage` for
  `RunDeferred`, as it does for `RunCompleted`.

### 4.8 Re-check on `Approved`

A second entry point on `RunContext`, next to `authorize_tool`, for example
`reauthorize_approved_tool(tool, effect, args)`. The rules (ADR-0028 (g)):

- Do not fire `PreToolUse` again.
- Run the deny rules, guard `Deny`, the mode and the policy again.
- `Defer`, `AskUser` and guard `Ask` count as answered by this approval. The
  approval handler is not called.
- Any `Deny` wins.
- A `Replace` with args that are different from the recorded args denies the
  call ("arguments changed on re-check"). A `Replace` with equal args passes.
- A tool that the agent does not have any more is denied with
  "tool no longer available". The tool lookup gives the `ToolEffect` for the
  mode check.
- The call runs on the recorded agent (§4.7).

The deferral flag (§4.2) has no effect on the re-check, because the re-check
cannot defer.

### 4.9 Temporal

`TemporalRunner` v0 does not support `Defer`:

- It sets the deferral flag to `false` (§4.2). The worker-built context has
  `false` by default, and `execute_tool_call` maps `Defer` to `Deny`.
- It rejects resolutions with `RunError::InvalidResume`.
- Its driver keeps its wildcard arms. It never sees the new transition input.

### 4.10 Compatibility and release

- All new variants and fields are on `#[non_exhaustive]` types. In-crate struct
  literals of `AgentInput` (for example the handoff in `agent.rs`) change with
  the new fields.
- The test `every_variant_covers_the_whole_enum` in `agent.rs` has a hard-coded
  variant count. It changes from 17 to 18.
- The changelog of `paigasus-helikon-core` says: "Once a host stores a
  `tool_deferred` event, it cannot roll back below this version, because an
  older reader cannot parse the row."
- Release: pure-auto release-plz, with no version bump by hand.
  `runtime-tokio` and `runtime-temporal` are already released, so release-plz
  publishes core first in one release PR (proven in SMA-418). The commit type is
  `feat(core)`. The PR title scope must be on `main`'s allowlist.
- Docs: update the mdBook page that describes permissions and approvals, and the
  core README if it shows the approval flow. The builder finds the pages.

## 5. Tests

- **Authorization unit tests** (`core/src/control.rs` `authorize_tests`):
  - a policy `Defer`;
